description: We are a team of young innovators participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission, we aim to make space data accessible through an interactive web experience that reveals how the universe changes over time. Combining technology, creativity, and collaboration, we turn complex astronomical data into discoveries everyone can explore. ✨
summary:
LUMEN is an astronomical data exploration platform designed to make complex space-mission data easier to access, understand, and analyze. By bringing together data from missions such as NASA's SPHEREx, ESA's Gaia, and Canada's NEOSSat, LUMEN provides a unified environment for exploring scientific observations.

The platform demonstrates scientific workflows through SPHEREx FITS image inspection and Gaia stellar data analysis, transforming raw astronomical measurements into meaningful visual representations. It aims to help users move beyond simply viewing space images and begin understanding the scientific information behind them.

LUMEN addresses the challenge of making rapidly growing astronomical datasets more accessible and usable. By simplifying data exploration while considering scientific accuracy, data quality, and scalability, the project aims to support astronomy education, encourage scientific curiosity, and make the exploration of our universe more approachable for everyone.
details:
LUMEN is an astronomical data exploration platform that brings data from SPHEREx, Gaia, and NEOSSat into one accessible environment. It helps users explore scientific observations, inspect FITS images, analyze stellar data, and transform complex astronomical datasets into meaningful visual insights.

Built using Python and modern web technologies, LUMEN aims to make real astronomical data easier to understand and explore for students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts.

Data Availability Notice: Due to GitHub's file size limitations, the large scientific datasets used by LUMEN could not be included in the repository. The datasets are therefore stored separately and are not part of the uploaded source code.
